question: In a certain code language, "CLOUD" is written as "FORXG." How will "SMILE" be written in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. VPLOH.

GIVEN

• CLOUD → FORXG.

SOLUTION

• Compare letter by letter: C → F (+3), L → O (+3), O → R (+3), U → X (+3), D → G (+3). Every letter is shifted 3 places forward.

• SMILE: S + 3 = V, M + 3 = P, I + 3 = L, L + 3 = O, E + 3 = H.

• So SMILE → VPLOH.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Check only the first two letters: S+3 = V, M+3 = P → only "VP…" in Option 2.

NOTE

• Option 1 (VLPOH) swaps the positions of M and I; Option 3 (VOLNH) and Option 4 (VONLH) have wrong letters at positions 2–4 (M → O/N is +2/+1, not +3).

• The candidate's recorded response in the source is Option 3 (marked wrong).

question: In a certain code language, "SILENCE" is written as "TLQFQHF." How will "SCIENCE" be written?
solution_text:

GIVEN

• SILENCE → TLQFQHF.

SOLUTION

• S → T (+1), I → L (+3), L → Q (+5), E → F (+1), N → Q (+3), C → H (+5), E → F (+1). The shifts follow the repeating pattern +1, +3, +5.

• SCIENCE: S+1 = T, C+3 = F, I+5 = N, E+1 = F, N+3 = Q, C+5 = H, E+1 = F.

• Code = TFNFQHF.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Pattern is +1, +3, +5, +1, +3, +5, +1 – apply to the new word position-wise. The last letter is E+1 = F, which eliminates Options 1 and 4.

NOTE

• Option 1 (TENEQHE) and Option 4 (TFNFQHE) end with E (the shift +1 would give F); Option 2 (TFNEQHF) has E at position 4 instead of F (E+1 = F).

question:
The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 7 : 9. After 8 years, the ratio becomes 9: 11.

What is the present age of A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 28 years.

GIVEN

• A : B = 7 : 9 (present); after 8 years A : B = 9 : 11.

SOLUTION

• Let present ages be 7x and 9x. After 8 years: (7x + 8)/(9x + 8) = 9/11.

• 11(7x + 8) = 9(9x + 8) → 77x + 88 = 81x + 72 → 4x = 16 → x = 4.

• Present age of A = 7 × 4 = 28 years (B = 36).

• Check: after 8 years: 36 and 44 → 36 : 44 = 9 : 11 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Difference of ages is constant: 2x = 2 parts now, and 2 parts after 8 years. Check options: for A = 28, B = 36; after 8 years 36 : 44 = 9 : 11 ✓.

NOTE

• Option 2 (35) → B = 45; after 8 years 43 : 53 ≠ 9 : 11. Option 3 (42) → B = 54; 50 : 62 ≠ 9 : 11. Option 4 (49) → B = 63; 57 : 71 ≠ 9 : 11.

question: If 24 men or 40 women can complete a work in 18 days, in how many days will 12 men and 20 women complete the same work?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 18 days.

GIVEN

• 24 men = 40 women (each can finish the work in 18 days).

SOLUTION

• 24 men = 40 women → 12 men = 20 women (half of both).

• So 12 men + 20 women = 20 women + 20 women = 40 women (or equivalently 24 men).

• 40 women finish the work in 18 days → 12 men and 20 women finish in 18 days.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• 12 men + 20 women = ½(24 men) + ½(40 women) = 24 men-equivalents or 40 women-equivalents → the same 18 days.

NOTE

• Option 1 (12 days) and Option 2 (14 days) assume more workers than available; Option 4 (22 days) assumes fewer.

• Total work = 24 × 18 = 432 man-days; 12 men + 20 women = 12 + 12 = 24 man-equivalents/day → 432/24 = 18 days.

question: A number is first increased by 40% and then decreased by 30%. If the final result is 784, what was the original number?
solution_text:

• Check: 800 × 1.4 = 1120; 1120 × 0.7 = 784 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

• Net change = +40 − 30 − (40 × 30)/100 = −2% → final = 98% of the original. 98% of 800 = 784.

NOTE

• Option 1 (760) → 745 final; Option 2 (780) → 764.4; Option 4 (840) → 823.2.

question:
The following symbols are used to denote family relationships:

1. P @ Q indicates that P is the mother of Q.

2. P # Q indicates that P is the father of Q.

3. P $ Q indicates that P is the sister of Q.

4. P % Q indicates that P is the son of Q.

Using the relationship pattern given above, identify how A is related to E in the given expression:

A @ B $ C % D # E
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Mother.

GIVEN

• A @ B → A is the mother of B. B $ C → B is the sister of C. C % D → C is the son of D. D # E → D is the father of E.

SOLUTION

• A is the mother of B, and B is the sister of C → A is also the mother of C.

• C is the son of D → D is the father of C, so A and D are the parents of C (A is D's wife).

• D is the father of E → E is a child of D; taking A as the mother of D's children, A is the mother of E.

• Verification flag: strictly, the expression establishes only that A is the wife of D and E is D's child; "Mother" (the key, Option 1) assumes that all of D's children are also A's. The key is retained as printed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Chain: A = mother of B & C; D = father of C & E → A and D are a couple with children B, C, E.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Wife): A is D's wife but not E's wife; Option 3 (Daughter-in-law): A is not married to a son of E's family in this chain; Option 4 (Sister): A is a parent generation, not E's sister.

question: Pointing at a photograph, X states, “I do not have any siblings. However, the father of that man is the son of my father.” Whose photograph is it?

SOLUTION

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• "Son of my father" with no siblings = "myself".

NOTE

• Option 1 (His own): would require "father of that man is my father" ("son of my father" would mean himself only if "that man" is his brother, which X lacks).

• Option 3 (His father's) would require "that man is the father of my father's son".

• Option 4 (His nephew's): a nephew needs a sibling, but X has none.

question:

question:

Statements

2. No pathogen is beneficial.

3. Some microorganisms are pathogens.

II. Some microorganisms are not beneficial.

III. All pathogens are viruses.

IV. Some beneficial organisms are not microorganisms.
option_2: Only I, II and IV follow
solution_text:

• III. "All pathogens are viruses" is the converse of statement 1 → ✗ does not follow.

• IV. Nothing is said about beneficial organisms that are not microorganisms ✗.

• Conclusions I and II follow → Option 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Combine statements: A + E → E (I); I + E → O (II). Converse of an "All" statement never follows (III); unrelated terms (IV) do not follow.

question:
Read the given statement carefully and the following assumptions based on it. Decide which of the assumptions are implicit in the statement.

Statement:

The city administration is considering a hike in parking fees to discourage people from bringing private cars into the city center.

Assumptions:

I. Every person who drives a car into the city does so only for entertainment purposes.

II. Public transport is currently functioning at full capacity and cannot handle more commuters.
option_1: Neither Assumption I nor II is implicit
option_4: Both Assumptions I and II are implicit
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Neither Assumption I nor II is implicit.

GIVEN

• Statement: the administration is considering a hike in parking fees to discourage private cars in the city centre.

SOLUTION

• Assumption I: "Every person… only for entertainment purposes" – an extreme, universal claim (every/only); the statement does not restrict car use to entertainment → not implicit.

• Assumption II: Public transport "at full capacity and cannot handle more commuters" – if this were true, discouraging cars would be unworkable; the plan instead assumes people can switch to alternatives → not implicit.

• Hence neither I nor II is implicit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

question:
Read the given statement carefully and the following assumptions based on it. Decide which of the assumptions are implicit in the statement.

Statement:

The insurance company has introduced a "Pay-as-you-drive" motor insurance policy, where the premium is calculated based on the actual distance the vehicle is driven, specifically targeting car owners who use their vehicles infrequently.

Assumptions:

I. The company assumes that by launching this innovative policy, it will be able to capture the entire market share of motor insurance from all competing firms within the very first fiscal year of the product's launch.

II. The company assumes that a substantial number of vehicle owners drive their cars significantly less than the average user and would find a usage-based premium financially more attractive than a standard, flat-rate insurance premium.
option_1: Both Assumptions I and II are implicit
option_3: Neither Assumption I nor II is implicit
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Only Assumption II is implicit.

GIVEN

• Statement: a "Pay-as-you-drive" policy is introduced for car owners who use their vehicles infrequently.

SOLUTION

• Assumption I: capturing the entire market from all competitors in the first year – an extreme, unrealistic claim; the statement only targets a specific group → not implicit.

• Assumption II: the company must believe that many owners drive little and will find a usage-based premium cheaper/more attractive; otherwise it would not launch the scheme → implicit.

• Hence only Assumption II is implicit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Extreme words (entire, all, very first) → reject. A reasonable assumption that explains why the action was taken → accept.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Both) wrongly accepts I; Option 2 (Only I) accepts the wrong assumption; Option 3 (Neither) rejects II, which is essential to the scheme's logic.

question: An object of height 4 cm is placed at a distance of 24 cm in front of a convex lens having a focal length of 10 cm. Which of the following accurately describes the position, height, and nature of the image formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 17.14 cm, 2.86 cm, Real and Inverted.

GIVEN

• Object height h = 4 cm; object distance u = −24 cm; focal length of convex lens f = +10 cm.

SOLUTION

• Lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f → 1/v = 1/10 + 1/(−24) = 1/10 − 1/24 = (12 − 5)/120 = 7/120.

• v = 120/7 ≈ 17.14 cm (positive → image on the other side of the lens → real).

• Magnification m = v/u = 17.14/(−24) = −0.714 (negative → inverted).

• Image height h′ = m × h = −0.714 × 4 = −2.86 cm (size 2.86 cm).

• Image: 17.14 cm, 2.86 cm, real and inverted.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Object beyond F (u = 24 > f = 10) but within 2F? 2F = 20 cm; the object is beyond 2F (24 cm > 20 cm), so the image lies between F and 2F (10 to 20 cm), is real, inverted and diminished → matches 17.14 cm and 2.86 cm (< 4 cm).

NOTE

• Option 2 and Option 4 describe virtual and erect images, which a convex lens forms only when the object is inside the focal length (u < f).

• Option 3 (7.14 cm, 1.43 cm) has an image closer than the focal length, which is impossible for a real image.

• Note: the candidate's recorded response in the source is Option 2 (marked wrong).

question:
A is sentenced to the following:

• rigorous imprisonment for 8 years,

• a fine of ₹20,000,

• and in default of payment, 1 year's simple imprisonment.

After serving 6 months of default imprisonment, A pays half the fine amount. Which of the following is correct under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India?
option_1: A must still complete the entire default imprisonment because imprisonment has already commenced.
option_2: A is immediately entitled to release because payment of half the fine automatically wipes out the sentence.
option_3: A must continue imprisonment only to the extent proportionate to the unpaid part of the fine.
option_4: The Court must conduct a fresh sentencing hearing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A must continue imprisonment only to the extent proportionate to the unpaid part of the fine..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 (which replaced the IPC 1860 w.e.f. 1 July 2024), the default imprisonment terminates when the fine is paid, and if a proportional part of the fine is paid, the imprisonment is reduced proportionately (corresponding to Sections 68–69 of the IPC; Sections 10–11 of BNS). (जुर्माना न देने पर कारावास)

 

• Here: default term 1 year for ₹20,000; half the fine paid → proportionate unpaid part = half → A must continue imprisonment only for the proportionate period (6 months), and since 6 months have already been served, A would then be entitled to release. The key states Option 3 – imprisonment continues only to the extent proportionate to the unpaid part of the fine.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• BNS has 358 sections; BNSS (replacing CrPC) has 531 sections; Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (replacing Evidence Act) has 170 sections.

 

• Punishments under BNS (Section 4): death, imprisonment for life, imprisonment (rigorous/simple), forfeiture of property, fine, and community service (new).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is wrong: imprisonment shrinks in proportion to part-payment; Option 2 is wrong: payment of part of the fine does not wipe out the whole sentence – only a proportionate part; Option 4 is wrong: no fresh sentencing hearing is required.

 

• Verification flag: the section numbers are given from the IPC–BNS correspondence; the key (Option 3) is retained.

question: Which of the following best distinguishes economics from many other social sciences?

question: Find the number of digits in the square root of 282429536481.

question: If p: q: r= 1: 3: 4 and 2p + q + 3r = 51, find the value of r.

question: A, B, and C enter into a partnership in which A’s capital is used for 5 months, and he claims 1/7 of the profit. B's capital is used for 7 months, and he claims 1/5 of the profit. If C invested ₹4,600 for 9 months, how much total capital was invested by A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ₹1,800.

GIVEN

• A: 5 months, profit share 1/7; B: 7 months, profit share 1/5; C: ₹4,600 for 9 months.

SOLUTION

• C's profit share = 1 − 1/7 − 1/5 = (35 − 5 − 7)/35 = 23/35.

• Profit ratio A : B : C = 5/35 : 7/35 : 23/35 = 5 : 7 : 23.

• Profit ∝ capital × time. C: 4,600 × 9 = 41,400 ↔ 23 parts → 1 part = 1,800.

• A's capital × 5 = 5 parts = 9,000 → A's capital = 9,000/5 = ₹1,800.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Capital × time ∝ profit share; A's (capital × 5) ÷ C's 41,400 = 5/23 → capital = 41,400 × 5/(23 × 5) = 1,800.

NOTE

• Option 2 (₹2,000), Option 3 (₹1,500) and Option 4 (₹2,100) do not satisfy the ratio 5 : 23 with C's 41,400.

question: The monthly income of Anita is ₹24,000, and her monthly expenditure is ₹16,000. If her income increases by 25% and her expenditure increases by 10%, find the percentage increase in her savings.

question: If a + b = 3 and ab = 2, find a³ + b³.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 9.

GIVEN

SOLUTION

• a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b).

• Check: a, b = 1, 2 → 1 + 8 = 9 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

• Roots of t² − 3t + 2 = 0 are 1 and 2 → 1³ + 2³ = 9.

question: If the side of a regular hexagon is doubled, what happens to its area?

question: A sum of ₹5,000 amounts to ₹6,500 in 3 years at simple interest. If the rate of interest is doubled, what will be the amount of the same sum in 5 years?
solution_text:

question: Given that the average of five consecutive odd numbers is 27, determine the product of the first and last numbers.

question: A manufacturer sells an item to a wholesale dealer at a profit of 10%. The wholesaler sells it to a retailer at a profit of 20%. If the retailer pays ₹1,320 for it, find the cost price for the manufacturer.

question: The area of a sector of a circle of radius 28 cm is 308 sq cm. Find the central angle of the sector. (Use π = 22/7)

question: A loan of ₹12,400 is taken at 10% compound interest, payable in two equal annual installments. Find the approximate installment amount.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ₹7,145.

NOTE

question: If 3 sin θ + 5 cos θ = 5, find the value of 5 sin θ − 3 cos θ.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ±3.

GIVEN

• Let x = 5 sin θ − 3 cos θ. Use (a sin θ + b cos θ)² + (b sin θ − a cos θ)² = a² + b².

• (3 sin θ + 5 cos θ)² + (5 sin θ − 3 cos θ)² = 3² + 5² = 34.

• 25 + x² = 34 → x² = 9 → x = ±3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

question: What is the value of [sin(18°) cos(72°) + sec(61°) sin(29°) + cos(18°) sin(72°) + cosec(61°) cos(29°)] / [sec²(48°) − cot²(42°)]?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• Numerator: sin 18° cos 72° + sec 61° sin 29° + cos 18° sin 72° + cosec 61° cos 29°; denominator: sec² 48° − cot² 42°.

SOLUTION

• sin 18° cos 72° + cos 18° sin 72° = sin(18° + 72°) = sin 90° = 1.

• sec 61° sin 29° = sec 61° cos 61° = 1 (sin 29° = cos 61°).

• cosec 61° cos 29° = cosec 61° sin 61° = 1 (cos 29° = sin 61°).

• Numerator = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

• Denominator: cot 42° = tan 48° → sec² 48° − tan² 48° = 1.

• Value = 3/1 = 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Complementary angles: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ; cot(90° − θ) = tan θ; identity sec² θ − tan² θ = 1.

NOTE

• Option 1 (0), Option 2 (1) and Option 3 (2) result from missing one or more of the three unit terms in the numerator.

question: If cosec θ + cot θ = p, then find the value of (p² − 1)/(p² + 1).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. cos θ.

GIVEN

• cosec θ + cot θ = p.

SOLUTION

• p = 1/sin θ + cos θ/sin θ = (1 + cos θ)/sin θ.

• p² − 1 = [(1 + cos θ)² − sin²θ]/sin²θ = [1 + 2cos θ + cos²θ − (1 − cos²θ)]/sin²θ = 2cos θ(1 + cos θ)/sin²θ.

• p² + 1 = [(1 + cos θ)² + sin²θ]/sin²θ = [2 + 2cos θ]/sin²θ = 2(1 + cos θ)/sin²θ.

• (p² − 1)/(p² + 1) = cos θ.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Test with θ = 90°: cosec = 1, cot = 0 → p = 1 → (1 − 1)/(1 + 1) = 0 = cos 90° ✓ (sin 90° = 1, tan 90° undefined, cot 90° = 0 – cot also gives 0; test with θ = 60°: p = 2/√3 + 1/√3 = √3 → (3 − 1)/(3 + 1) = 1/2 = cos 60° ✓ (cot 60° = 0.577 ✗)).

NOTE

• Option 1 (sin θ = 0.866 at 60°), Option 2 (tan θ = 1.732) and Option 4 (cot θ = 0.577) do not equal 1/2 at θ = 60°. The candidate's recorded response in the source is Option 4 (marked wrong).

question: The ratio of the volumes of two hemispheres is 27 : 64. What is the ratio of their total surface areas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 9:16.

GIVEN

• V₁ : V₂ = 27 : 64 for two hemispheres.

SOLUTION

• Volume of hemisphere = (2/3)πr³ → V ∝ r³ → r₁³ : r₂³ = 27 : 64 → r₁ : r₂ = 3 : 4.

• Total surface area of a hemisphere = 3πr² → TSA ∝ r².

• Ratio of TSA = 3² : 4² = 9 : 16.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Volume ratio = (ratio of radii)³ → radii 3 : 4 → area ratio = (radii ratio)² = 9 : 16.

NOTE

• Option 1 (3:4) is the ratio of radii; Option 3 (27:64) is the ratio of volumes; Option 4 (81:256) is the fourth power of the radius ratio.

question: Evaluate the value of the expression: 3(sin θ − cos θ)⁴ + 6(sin θ + cos θ)² + 4(sin⁶ θ + cos⁶ θ).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 13.

GIVEN

• E = 3(sin θ − cos θ)⁴ + 6(sin θ + cos θ)² + 4(sin⁶ θ + cos⁶ θ).

SOLUTION

• Let t = sin θ cos θ.

• (sin θ − cos θ)² = 1 − 2t → (sin θ − cos θ)⁴ = 1 − 4t + 4t² → 3(…) = 3 − 12t + 12t².

• (sin θ + cos θ)² = 1 + 2t → 6(…) = 6 + 12t.

• sin⁶ θ + cos⁶ θ = 1 − 3t² → 4(…) = 4 − 12t².

• Sum: (3 + 6 + 4) + (−12t + 12t) + (12t² − 12t²) = 13.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Put θ = 0°: 3(0 − 1)⁴ + 6(0 + 1)² + 4(0 + 1) = 3 + 6 + 4 = 13.

NOTE

• Option 1 (1), Option 2 (7) and Option 4 (10) result from missing terms (e.g., 6 + 4 = 10).

• Identities: sin⁶θ + cos⁶θ = 1 − 3sin²θcos²θ; sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ = 1 − 2sin²θcos²θ.

question: In a triangle ABC, D and E are points on sides AB and AC respectively such that DE ∥ BC. If AD = x, DB = x-2, AE = x+2, and EC = x-1, find the value of x.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 4.

GIVEN

• DE ∥ BC; AD = x, DB = x − 2, AE = x + 2, EC = x − 1.

SOLUTION

• By the Basic Proportionality (Thales) theorem: AD/DB = AE/EC.

• x/(x − 2) = (x + 2)/(x − 1) → x(x − 1) = (x + 2)(x − 2).

• x² − x = x² − 4 → x = 4.

• Check: AD = 4, DB = 2, AE = 6, EC = 3 → 4/2 = 6/3 = 2 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Substitute the options: x = 4 gives 4/2 = 6/3 ✓.

NOTE

• Option 2 (x = 2) makes DB = 0; Option 3 (x = 10) gives 10/8 ≠ 12/9; Option 4 (x = 7) gives 7/5 ≠ 9/6. The candidate's recorded response in the source is Option 2 (marked wrong).

question: In a circle with centre O and radius 13 cm, two parallel chords AB and CD are drawn on opposite sides of the centre. If AB = 10 cm and CD = 24 cm, find the distance between the two chords (in cm).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 17 cm.

GIVEN

• Radius = 13 cm; AB = 10 cm; CD = 24 cm; chords parallel and on opposite sides of the centre.

SOLUTION

• Distance of a chord from the centre = √(r² − (half chord)²).

• For AB: √(13² − 5²) = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12 cm.

• For CD: √(13² − 12²) = √(169 − 144) = √25 = 5 cm.

• Opposite sides of the centre → distance between the chords = 12 + 5 = 17 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Pythagorean triples (5, 12, 13): the distances are 12 and 5 → 12 + 5 = 17.

NOTE

• Option 1 (15 cm) and Option 3 (21 cm) are not combinations of 12 and 5 (12 − 5 = 7 would apply if on the same side); Option 4 (25 cm) = 12 + 13.

question: A bucket contains a mixture of two liquids P and Q are in the ratio 4 : 1. When 10 liters of the mixture is taken out and 10 liters of liquid Q is poured into the bucket, the ratio becomes 2 : 3. How many liters of liquid P was contained in the bucket?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 16 liters.

GIVEN

• P : Q = 4 : 1 initially; 10 L removed; 10 L of Q added; new ratio P : Q = 2 : 3.

SOLUTION

• Let the total initial mixture = T litres. P = 4T/5, Q = T/5.

• After removing 10 L: P = (4/5)(T − 10), Q = (1/5)(T − 10).

• After adding 10 L of Q: P = (4/5)(T − 10); Q = (1/5)(T − 10) + 10.

• Ratio 2 : 3 → 3 × (4/5)(T − 10) = 2[(1/5)(T − 10) + 10] → (12/5)(T − 10) = (2/5)(T − 10) + 20.

• 2(T − 10) = 20 → T = 20.

• P initially = (4/5) × 20 = 16 litres.

• Check: after removing 10 L of the 20 L mixture, P = 8 L, Q = 2 L; after adding 10 L of Q: P = 8 L, Q = 12 L → 8 : 12 = 2 : 3 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Work with fractions: P left = 0.8(T − 10); Q left = 0.2(T − 10) + 10.

NOTE

• Hence the bucket originally contained 16 L of P and 4 L of Q (Option 2).

• Option 1 (14), Option 3 (18) and Option 4 (20) do not give the ratio 2 : 3 after the operation.

question: The diagonal of the square base of a right square pyramid is 10√2 cm. If the lateral surface area of the pyramid is 260 cm², calculate the volume of the pyramid.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 400 cm³.

GIVEN

• Diagonal of the square base = 10√2 cm; lateral surface area = 260 cm².

SOLUTION

• Side of the base a = diagonal/√2 = 10 cm.

• Lateral surface area = 4 × (1/2) × a × l = 2al = 2 × 10 × l = 20l = 260 → slant height l = 13 cm.

• Height h = √(l² − (a/2)²) = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12 cm.

• Volume = (1/3) × a² × h = (1/3) × 100 × 12 = 400 cm³.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• (5, 12, 13) triple → height 12; volume = 100 × 12/3 = 400.

NOTE

• Option 2 (300), Option 3 (450) and Option 4 (350) correspond to heights of 9, 13.5 and 10.5 cm, which do not match l = 13 and a/2 = 5.

question: A shopkeeper marks a shirt at ₹1200 and offers a discount of 15%. He marks a pair of trousers at ₹2000 and offers a discount of 25%. If a customer buys 3 shirts and 2 trousers, find the approximate overall discount percentage on the total purchase.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 20.26%.

GIVEN

• Shirt: marked ₹1200, discount 15%; trousers: marked ₹2000, discount 25%; 3 shirts + 2 trousers.

SOLUTION

• Marked price of 3 shirts = 3 × 1200 = ₹3,600; discount = 15% of 3,600 = ₹540.

• Marked price of 2 trousers = 2 × 2000 = ₹4,000; discount = 25% of 4,000 = ₹1,000.

• Total marked price = ₹7,600; total discount = ₹1,540.

• Overall discount % = (1,540/7,600) × 100 = 20.26% (approx.).

question: Two circles intersect at points P and Q. Their common tangents AB and CD meet the line PQ, extended on both sides, at points X and Y respectively. If PQ = 8 cm and XY = 17 cm, find the length of AB (in cm).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 15 cm.

GIVEN

• Circles intersect at P and Q; PQ = 8 cm. Direct common tangents AB and CD meet line PQ (extended) at X and Y; XY = 17 cm.

SOLUTION

• The line PQ is the common chord (radical axis). Let M be the midpoint of PQ. The two tangents are mirror images about the line of centres, which passes through M, so XM = YM = 17/2 = 8.5 cm.

• Power of the point X: XA² = XP × XQ = (XM − 4)(XM + 4) = XM² − 16 = 72.25 − 16 = 56.25.

• Also, X is the midpoint of AB (XA = XB, since XA² = XP·XQ = XB²), so XA = 7.5 cm and AB = 2 × 7.5 = 15 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• (AB/2)² = (XY/2)² − (PQ/2)² = 8.5² − 4² = 56.25 → AB/2 = 7.5 → AB = 15 (8-15-17 triple: 8.5² = 4² + 7.5²).

NOTE

• Option 1 (12), Option 2 (13) and Option 3 (14) do not satisfy (AB/2)² = 56.25 (they give AB/2 = 6, 6.5, 7).

question: If x + 1/x = 9, then find the value of x³ + 1/x³ + x² + 1/x².
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 781.

GIVEN

• x + 1/x = 9.

SOLUTION

• x² + 1/x² = (x + 1/x)² − 2 = 81 − 2 = 79.

• x³ + 1/x³ = (x + 1/x)³ − 3(x + 1/x) = 729 − 27 = 702.

• Required value = 702 + 79 = 781.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Remember: x² + 1/x² = p² − 2; x³ + 1/x³ = p³ − 3p, where p = x + 1/x.

NOTE

• Option 1 (702) is only x³ + 1/x³; Option 2 (729) is 9³; Option 3 (779) = 702 + 77 (using x² + 1/x² = 77 – forgetting that 81 − 2 = 79).

question: A point P is at a distance of 13 cm from the center of a circle. If the radius of the circle is 5 cm, what is the length of the tangent segment drawn from point P to the circle?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 12 cm.

SOLUTION

• The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact → triangle OTP is right-angled at T.
